items.title: New Bronzeville Development Will Only Displace Residents If New Bears Stadium Is Part Of Project
items.description: Developers say that 1,000 Prairie Shores residents would be displaced if Bears stadium plans are successfully incorporated into the proposed Bronzeville Lakefront development.

items.title: Airplane Departures Resume After National Ground Stop Halted Flights At O’Hare, Midway Airports
items.description: Flights were canceled at both O'Hare and Midway amid a nationwide ground stop caused by communication problems, according to the Federal Aviation Administration.

items.title: Trader Joe’s Uptown Store Opens Monday
items.description: The Far North Side has been clamoring for a Trader Joe's location for years.

items.title: Chicago’s Thanksgiving Parade Will Start Earlier This Year. Here’s What To Know
items.description: The parade steps off at 7:45 a.m. — an hour earlier than in recent years — with former Bears great Charles "Peanut" Tillman leading and a new Cookie Monster balloon.

items.title: North Lawndale Rallies Behind Monday Coffee After Break-In: ‘We Won’t Let Another Fail’
items.description: The cafe had a window smashed, doors damaged and equipment broken Thursday, but a Gofundme was already well on its way to meeting a $12,000 goal.

items.title: City’s CFO Resigns Rather Than ‘Compromise My Integrity,’ Sparking Calls For Investigation
items.description: Ashlee Gabrysch took the role in August. Her resignation comes in the middle of yet another budget stalemate between the City Council and Mayor Brandon Johnson.

items.title: Peoples Gas Customers To See $56 Back In November Bill Credits
items.description: The credits come from a $125 million settlement reached with the attorney general’s office.

items.title: Ald. William Hall Is Running Against 2 Challengers In 6th Ward Race — For Now
items.description: Hall will compete against Allyson Renee Scrutchens and Curtiss Llong Bey, though the incumbent alderman and Llong Bey both face challenges to their nominating petitions.
